reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I should check the order and refund data myself rather than relying only on the handoff note. I'll start by listing the orders.
Orders are listed. Next I'll check the refunds list to confirm what has actually been applied before computing any balances.

The refunds list matches the handoff exactly: orders 170, 172 and 175 with the same amounts. Every order maps to a customer (acme, birch, cobalt), so I'll get each customer's net balance from net_balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance of 11259 matches my check: orders 170 and 173 total 28386, less the 17127 refund on order 170, leaves 11259. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net of 18633 matches my check: orders 171 and 174 total 18633 with no refunds against them. Cobalt is the last customer, so I'll get its net balance next.

Cobalt's net of 54502 matches my check: orders 172 and 175 total 64994, less refunds of 7535 and 2957, leaves 54502. All three balances reconcile with the orders and refunds, so I'll record the payouts, starting with acme at 11259.
Acme's payout of 11259 is recorded and reconciles with the orders and refunds. Birch's net of 18633 also reconciles, so I'll record its payout next.
Birch's payout of 18633 is recorded. The only remaining customer is cobalt, whose net of 54502 reconciles with orders 172 and 175 less their refunds, so I'll record that payout.
All three customers have been paid, and each payout reconciles with the orders and refunds I checked. The batch is complete, so I'll report the payouts.
